stated: Labour will improve animal welfare by banning trail hunting, the import of hunting trophies, puppy smuggling and farming, and the use of snare traps. They will also partner with scientists and industry to work towards phasing out animal testing.

source.quote: Labour will improve animal welfare. We will ban trail hunting and the import of hunting trophies. We will end puppy smuggling and farming, along with the use of snare traps. And we will partner with scientists, industry, and civil society as we work towards the phasing out of animal testing.

bearing_set.reason: The snare trap ban and trail hunting ban directly affect UK wildlife populations and biodiversity — snares are documented to kill non-target and protected species, so a ban earns a real verdict on O6's 'nature' component.

Working towards phasing out animal testing bears concretely on the drug development pipeline — animal models underpin preclinical safety/efficacy trials for new medicines and vaccines — so the pace and adequacy of alternative methods will materially affect the rate at which new treatments reach patients, a genuine (if contested) effect on healthcare access indicators.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O6 through direct biodiversity/nature effects of the snare and trophy provisions, and O3 through the animal-testing phase-out's effect on pharmaceutical R&D. The other provisions (puppy smuggling/farming ban, trail hunting ban) are primarily animal welfare measures without non-negligible effects on the people-centred fundamentals at population scale; any liberty cost (O10) of banning previously lawful activities is real but targeted at small communities and does not plausibly move a population-level O10 indicator materially.
